knowledge_claims.claim: The period generated 397 A/B leads and 58 Tier A leads.
knowledge_claims.interpretation: Because A/B density stays near 30 percent while volume grows, scaling improved absolute qualified volume but not quality density.
knowledge_claims.limitation_or_uncertainty: No CRM revenue validation is available.

knowledge_claims.claim: Intent signals separate high-quality and low-quality leads.
knowledge_claims.interpretation: The evidence explains that explicit trip readiness, especially tickets and near travel windows, is materially more associated with A/B and Tier A quality.
knowledge_claims.limitation_or_uncertainty: This is association, not causal proof.

knowledge_claims.claim: COMMERCIAL matched supports direct cost-quality reading.
knowledge_claims.interpretation: COMMERCIAL can be interpreted economically because the matched universe links spend and leads; ATTENTION and ACTIVATION are not equivalent decision layers.
knowledge_claims.limitation_or_uncertainty: Cross-layer KPI ranking is not allowed by the FARO profile.

knowledge_claims.interpretation: The concentration implies a practical testing focus, but it does not prove that creative content caused quality outcomes.

analytical_narrative.text: Lead quality is primarily separated by observable intent, while economics must remain inside the governed COMMERCIAL matched universe.
analytical_narrative.phenomenon: Volume scaled in June while A/B density stayed stable.
analytical_narrative.trade_off: Scaling volume without stronger intent filters increases C/D burden.
analytical_narrative.dominant_risk: Using a universal KPI across FARO layers would misread strategic roles.
analytical_narrative.strategic_implication: Protect commercial acquisition and test intent filters before declaring optimization winners.

limitations: No revenue or CRM final outcome source.
